text.p: Bonds closed at their highs but the longer end would probably needed a fresh boost from Spain to advance further on Thursday, traders said.

Prices had been given a lift by better-than-expected inflation figures for October, with the month-on-month rate dipping 0.1 percent. Concern about inflation had been seen as one factor restraining any quick cut in rates by the Bank of Portugal.
"Tomorrow, we are going to see another session in which the trend is set in Spain," said one trader.

Traders said that the market was well-supported but that the 10-year cash was reaching a zone in which profit-taking could be seen. "7.25 percent is an area for profit-taking that could brake further rises," said another trader.
Another trader said that the spread with Spain would remain between 10 and 15 basis points for the 10 year.
Traders said the inflation news was well-received at the short end of the curve but investors remained cautious on whether the Bank of Portugal would cut rates in the near term.
